title: dedicated-autoscaler-tokenbucket-smoothing-util-reporting-fix
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets were experiencing short, repeated bursts that caused oscillation in token-bucket based autoscalers. The smoothing parameters and telemetry were insufficient to diagnose and guarantee throughput for bursty workloads. This PR smooths token-bucket refill behavior, exposes additional utilization metrics for fleet-level dashboards, and fixes a bug where short-lived bursts were double-counted in the utilization window.

What I changed: 1) Introduced a moving-average based smoothing layer for token refill rates to reduce oscillation during bursty traffic. 2) Fixed counting logic that led to double-counting of queued tokens when tasks were requeued on transient failures. 3) Added new metrics: dedicated_autoscaler_burst_util_pct, dedicated_autoscaler_burst_queue_depth, dedicated_autoscaler_effective_refill_rps. 4) Exposed a new per-fleet utilization summary to the console (dashboard JSON) and updated the Prometheus metrics and alerts. 5) Added unit and integration tests that reproduce the bursty pattern and validate stability and throughput guarantees.

Backwards compatibility: All public autoscaler configs are additive. New smoothing config defaults to previous behavior (no smoothing) unless enabled by operator. Dashboard/alert names are additive; alerts referencing the old utilization metric continue to work.

Related work: builds on ENG-4021 (autoscaler tokenbucket refactor) and complements recent utilization reporting changes in pr-302500 and pr-318999.

release_notes:
- Improve autoscaler stability for short bursts by adding token-bucket smoothing (config opt-in).
- Fix double-counting bug that inflated utilization during transient requeues.
- Add three new metrics: dedicated_autoscaler_burst_util_pct, dedicated_autoscaler_burst_queue_depth, dedicated_autoscaler_effective_refill_rps.
- Dashboard: add Dedicated Fleet Utilization summary and example alert thresholds.
notes_for_ops: Operators can enable smoothing via the new config: autoscaler.smoothing.enabled=true and tune smoothing.window_ms (default: 0). Default behavior unchanged. New metrics are available under prometheus job=redwood-autoscaler. If you see decreased throughput after enabling smoothing, tune smoothing.alpha (0.0-1.0) and refill_rps_override per-fleet.
qa_plan: Unit tests cover smoothing logic and double-count fix. Integration test drives a deterministic burst pattern (3 bursts @200ms, 5s interval) and asserts smoothing keeps utilization variance <3% over 60s. Manual QA: deploy to staging with a 2-node dedicated fleet, enable smoothing, and run the 'burst-suite' load generator for 10 minutes while collecting metrics and traces.
